title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed English sheet, numbered N27, that Grothendieck filed among his handwritten notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. The previous page is handwritten French on forms on simplices Δ_n, face maps Δ_0→Δ_1 and Δ_2→Δ_1, and augmented differential algebras. The typed sheet is an expository passage on Sullivan's minimal models. Its wording ('Hirsch calculation described in Appendix H', 'Λ_{1,n}', 'over Q and R') indicates a mid-1970s circulated Sullivan text or lecture notes (Sullivan or someone close to him), not Grothendieck's own work. I cannot securely identify the exact source.

In modern language the page says the following.
(1) Let Λ be the minimal Sullivan model of a space X. Let Λ_1 be its 1-stage part, generated in degree 1, and Λ_{1,n} the sub-dga after n steps of Hirsch extensions. Then Λ_{1,n} determines the Malcev completion of the nilpotent quotient π_1/Γ_n π_1 (lower central series), over Q or R. Dually, the Lie algebra of π_1/C_n ⊗ Q is the dual of the generators of Λ_{1,n}.
(2) The minimal model is built purely algebraically and inductively:
- Λ_1 is built to give an isomorphism on H^1 and an injection on H^2.
- Degree-2 generators are added in a possibly infinite sequence of Hirsch extensions. The first step makes H^2 an isomorphism; the later steps make H^3 injective.
- Then degree 3, degree 4, and so on.
(3) Over Q, applying spatial realization to these Hirsch extensions gives a Postnikov-type tower of principal fibrations. Each fibre is an Eilenberg–MacLane space K(V,n) with V a rational vector space. This tower is taken as the rational homotopy type of X for any fundamental group.
(4) The meaning of the higher-degree structure of the model for non-nilpotent spaces is said to be 'not yet completely understood except in a philosophical way'.

Context for the archive: Grothendieck's 1976 IHÉS lecture concerned a divided-power analogue, over Z, of the de Rham algebra on simplices. Sullivan's polynomial forms on Δ_n would be replaced by forms with divided powers, aiming at an integral analogue of Sullivan's theory. That explains why this exposition sits among his notes.
errors: No mathematical errors; the description of the minimal-model construction is standard.

The claim that the tower is 'the rational homotopy type of the space ... defined in general for all spaces regardless of the fundamental group' needs qualification. For non-nilpotent spaces the Sullivan model sees only a nilpotent/pro-unipotent completion, not the homotopy type in any naive sense. The text itself partly acknowledges this.

missed.claim: Archival/historical: Grothendieck read Sullivan's minimal-model exposition alongside his own 1976 work on a divided-power (integral) de Rham complex on simplices. This documents that his project was conceived as an integral counterpart of Sullivan's rational theory. The page contains no new mathematics by Grothendieck.
missed.quote: the minimal model Λ of the de Rham algebra is constructed in a purely algebriac computational construction
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's engagement with rational homotopy theory before Pursuing Stacks. That is relevant to histories of integral and p-adic homotopy models (later Cenkl–Porter, Mandell, Lurie, Toën).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typed copy of standard Sullivan minimal-model exposition, not Grothendieck's text. Its only interest is the archival fact that he studied it during his divided-power de Rham work.
transcription_corrections: 'algebriac' is a typo in the original typescript (should be 'algebraic'); the transcription is faithful.
The handwritten '108' at the bottom is the archive page number, not part of the text.
